---
title: "RT Plots"
output: html_notebook
---

This script will relate the DDM parameters for each subject with their ideological variables.

# Libraries

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(data.table)
# Load necessary library
library(ggplot2)
```

# Plotting Reaction time Distributions

```{r}
# Calculate the mean and standard error (SE) for each gain value
average_data <- risk_data %>%
  group_by(gain) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_rt = mean(rt, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_rt = sd(rt, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())  # Standard error
  )

# Create the plot showing the average line with error bars
ggplot(average_data, aes(x = gain, y = mean_rt)) +
  geom_line(color = "red", size = 1) +                # Add red line for the average
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_rt - se_rt, ymax = mean_rt + se_rt), 
                width = 0.2, color = "black") +       # Add error bars
  labs(x = "Gain", y = "Average Reaction Time (RT)", title = "Average Gain vs Reaction Time with Error Bars") +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  theme_minimal()                                    # Use a minimal theme
 
```

```{r}
# Filter the data to include only rows where experimental_treatment_selected is "Yes to treatment"
filtered_data <- risk_data %>%
  filter(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment")

# Calculate the mean and standard error (SE) for each gain value
average_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(gain) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_rt = mean(rt, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_rt = sd(rt, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())  # Standard error
  )

# Create the plot showing the average line with error bars and horizontal caps
ggplot(average_data, aes(x = gain, y = mean_rt)) +
  geom_line(color = "red", size = 1) +                # Add red line for the average
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_rt - se_rt, ymax = mean_rt + se_rt), 
                width = 0.1, color = "black") +       # Add error bars with horizontal caps
  labs(x = "Gain", y = "Average Reaction Time (RT)", title = "Average Gain vs Reaction Time (Filtered)") +
  theme_minimal()                                    # Use a minimal theme
```
